## Build
Work inside `9999_init.sql` sections (8)–(11), `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` (one local-only tweak), `supabase/tests/helpers.sql`, `supabase/tests/rls/{01_tenancy,08_rerunnable,09_grants}.sql`, `scripts/db/test.sh`, plus the docs/handoff edits in Finish.

1. **Section (8) RLS baseline** — copy the DESIGN §4.4 block: the `do $$` loop that runs `alter table public.%I enable row level security` for every table in `pg_tables where schemaname = 'public'` (NO `force`: the owner-bypass scheme requires it). Then make table privileges explicit instead of relying on Supabase's default privileges (the local shim has none): `grant select, insert, update, delete on all tables in schema public to authenticated; grant all on all tables in schema public to service_role; revoke all on all tables in schema public from anon; revoke all on all tables in schema private from anon, authenticated, service_role;` (add `revoke usage on schema private` here if section (1) lacks it). Then the column-level block verbatim from DESIGN §4.4: `revoke all on public.persons, public.households from authenticated;` followed by `grant select (id, org_id, household_id, user_id, first_name, last_name, preferred_name, sex, household_role, congregation_status, directory_listed, photo_path, email, mobile_phone, work_phone, deceased_on, marital_status, birthdate_visibility, created_at, updated_at) on public.persons to authenticated;` and `grant select (id, org_id, name, address_line1, address_line2, city, region, postal_code, country, home_phone, photo_path, sort_key, created_at, updated_at) on public.households to authenticated;` (no `birthdate`, `member_since`, `youth_override`, `anniversary`, privacy flags, `privacy_confirmed_*`, `created_via`). Then the RPC-only `revoke insert, update, delete … from authenticated` verbatim from DESIGN (persons, households, both leader-notes tables, org_memberships, org_membership_permissions, invitations, join_codes, join_requests, sermon_share_links, billing_customers, billing_subscriptions, stripe_events, notifications, notification_deliveries, audit_log, storage_deletions, account_deletion_requests, super_admins). Re-issue `grant select on public.directory_households, public.directory_persons, public.org_directory_info to authenticated;` (views are owned by the migration owner, so they read the base tables with owner privileges; the functions they call — `app.household_view_level`, `app.is_adult`, `app.member_org_ids`, `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids` — are executed with the CALLER's privileges, which is why section (9) grants them to `authenticated`).
2. **Section (8) policy catalogue** — one `drop policy if exists <name> on <table>;` immediately before each `create policy`, names `ca_<table>_<op>_<who>`, every write policy also requires `app.org_writable(org_id)`, and viewer facts always in the InitPlan form `org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids()))` / `org_id = any((select app.perm_org_ids('<perm>')))` (never a correlated call per row). `service_role` gets no policies (BYPASSRLS). Implement DESIGN §6's table:
   - `organizations`: select `ca_orgs_select_fellowship` (verbatim from DESIGN: member or `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids()`); insert/update `ca_organizations_insert_super` / `ca_organizations_update_super` (`app.is_super_admin()`); no delete policy (`cancelled` + purge).
   - `organization_settings`: select member (`ca_organization_settings_select_member`); update `ca_organization_settings_update_org_settings` = `org.settings` ∧ writable; no insert/delete policy (the `on_org_created` trigger inserts as definer).
   - `fellowships` / `fellowship_memberships`: select when the caller is a member of a linked org (`exists (select 1 from public.fellowship_memberships fm where fm.fellowship_id = <id> and fm.org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids())))`) or super admin; insert/update/delete super only.
   - `profiles`: `ca_profiles_select_org_admin` verbatim from DESIGN (own row, or a `users.create`/`users.delete`/`users.edit_permissions` holder of a shared org); insert/update own row (`user_id = auth.uid()`); no delete.
   - `super_admins`: select super only; no writes (bootstrap INSERT runs as `postgres`).
   - `org_memberships`, `org_membership_permissions`: select own row (`user_id = auth.uid()`, via the membership for the permissions table) or any `users.*` holder of the org; no write policies (RPC-only; the revoke above already removes the privilege — the absence of policies is the second lock).
   - `invitations`, `join_codes`: select `users.create`; `join_requests`: select `users.create` or own (`user_id = auth.uid()`); no write policies.
   - `households` / `persons`: `ca_households_select_visible` / `ca_persons_select_visible` = `exists (select 1 from public.directory_households d where d.id = households.id)` (DESIGN: "base table only through the view's rule"); no write policies. `household_leader_notes` / `person_leader_notes`: select `org_id = any((select app.directory_admin_org_ids()))`; no write policies.
   - `audience_groups`: select member; insert/update/delete `announcements.create` or `org.settings` ∧ writable, and delete additionally `kind = 'custom'` (system rows are never deleted). `audience_group_members`: select, insert, delete for the same manager pair only; no update policy.
   - `calendars`: select member ∧ `app.user_in_group(view_audience_group_id)`; insert/update/delete `org.settings` ∧ writable.
   - `events`: select member ∧ calendar visible (`exists (select 1 from public.calendars c where c.id = events.calendar_id)` — the calendar policy applies inside the subquery) ∧ (`status = 'approved'` ∨ `submitted_by = auth.uid()` ∨ `announcements.edit`); insert member ∧ writable ∧ (`organization_settings.members_can_submit_events` ∨ `announcements.create`) ∧ `app.user_in_group(<calendar's submit_audience_group_id>)` ∧ `submitted_by = auth.uid()` (the 1.3a trigger forces `pending`/`push = false` for non-creators); update `using` own-while-pending or `announcements.edit`, `with check` the same plus `status = 'pending'` unless `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete` or own pending.
   - `sermons`: `ca_sermons_select_members` and `ca_sermons_insert_by_kind` verbatim from DESIGN §4.4; `ca_sermons_update_by_kind` with the same media-kind split in both `using` and `with check`; `ca_sermons_delete_sermons_delete` = `sermons.delete` ∧ writable.
   - `sermon_share_links`: select `sermons.link` or `sermons.upload`; no write policies (RPC-only).
   - `announcements`: select member ∧ `publish_at <= now()` ∧ (`expires_at is null or expires_at > now()`) ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or any of `announcements.create/edit/delete`; insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete` — each ∧ writable.
   - `bulletins`: select member ∧ `publish_at <= now()`, or `bulletins.upload`; insert/update/delete `bulletins.upload` ∧ writable. `documents`: select member ∧ published ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or `documents.upload`; writes `documents.upload` ∧ writable.
   - `surveys`, `survey_questions`: select member ∧ `status = 'open'` ∧ inside `[opens_at, closes_at]` (nulls open-ended) ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or any of `announcements.create/edit/delete` (questions via `exists` on the parent survey); insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit` (the 1.3a `freeze_survey_shape` trigger guards the shape); delete `announcements.delete`.
   - `survey_responses`: select own (`person_id = app.my_person_id(org_id)` or `household_id = any((select app.my_household_ids()))`) or the three announcement permissions; insert member ∧ writable ∧ survey open/in window/in audience (the `stamp_response_scope` trigger overwrites the scope columns); update own ∧ survey open ∧ `allow_edit` (per_household → any adult of the household through `my_household_ids`); no delete. `survey_answers`: select/insert/update through `exists` on the visible/own response with the same conditions; no delete.
   - `push_devices`, `notification_preferences`: one `for all` policy each, `using`/`with check` `user_id = auth.uid()` (preferences additionally `org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids()))` in `with check`).
   - `notifications`: select for any `announcements.*` holder; no write policies. `notification_deliveries`, `stripe_events`, `storage_deletions`: select super admin only. `billing_customers`, `billing_subscriptions`: select `org.settings` or super. `audit_log`: select `org.settings` or super; no writes (trigger-fed as definer). `account_deletion_requests`: select own.
   Every public table ends up with at least one select policy.
3. **Section (9) grants** — copy the DESIGN §4.4 block verbatim: `revoke execute on all functions in schema public from public, anon, authenticated; revoke execute on all functions in schema app from public, anon, authenticated;` then the three `grant execute` statements: the `app.*` helper list to `authenticated` (add `app.can_read_object(text, text)` and `app.can_write_object(text, text)` because the storage policies call them as the querying role; add `app.person_in_group(uuid, uuid)` only if a policy references it directly), the 17 client RPCs to `authenticated` with DESIGN's exact signatures (`my_context`, `set_membership_permissions`, `set_membership_status`, `remove_membership`, `create_invitation`, `revoke_invitation`, `accept_invitation`, `save_household`, `save_person`, `delete_person`, `set_household_privacy`, `save_leader_notes`, `set_congregation_status`, `create_share_link`, `revoke_share_link`, `submit_survey_response`, `request_account_deletion`), and the 7 `srv_*` RPCs to `service_role` only (`srv_resolve_share_link`, `srv_audience_user_ids`, `srv_enqueue_due_notifications`, `srv_claim_notifications`, `srv_attach_user`, `srv_process_account_deletions`, `srv_housekeeping`). If a 1.3b signature differs from DESIGN's, the grant must match the real function (grants on a non-existent signature fail the paste) and the difference goes to HANDOFF. `anon` receives nothing. Trigger functions, `app.require_*`, `app.rate_limit_*`, `app.person_in_kind` and every `srv_*` stay unreachable for `authenticated`.
4. **Section (10) storage** — start with the single constant: a `do $$ declare c_sermon_media_limit bigint := 52428800; -- 50 MiB: Supabase FREE plan cap (founder decision 10). On Pro raise the project's global upload limit in the dashboard, set this to 2147483648 (2 GiB) and re-paste this section; bucket rows are upserted. Keep NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB (docs/ENV.md) in sync. begin … end $$;` block that executes the `insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types) values … on conflict (id) do update set public = excluded.public, file_size_limit = excluded.file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types = excluded.allowed_mime_types` statement from DESIGN §4.4 with these rows: `sermon-media` (`c_sermon_media_limit`, MIME `audio/mpeg, audio/mp4, audio/aac, audio/ogg, audio/wav, audio/x-m4a, video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/webm`), `bulletins` (26214400; `application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png`), `documents` (52428800; the DESIGN allow-list: pdf, jpeg, png, text/plain, msword, docx, xls, xlsx), `directory-photos` (10485760; jpeg, png, webp), `org-assets` (5242880; jpeg, png, webp — no SVG). All `public = false`. Then the two policies: `drop policy if exists ca_storage_select on storage.objects; create policy ca_storage_select on storage.objects for select to authenticated using (app.can_read_object(bucket_id, name));` and `ca_storage_insert … for insert to authenticated with check (app.can_write_object(bucket_id, name));` — NO update/delete policies for `authenticated` (DESIGN §6: deletions only via `storage_deletions` + service role). Do not `enable row level security` on `storage.objects` in the migration (Supabase already has it; `postgres` does not own the table) — the shim does it locally (item 6).
5. **Section (11) bootstrap** — the commented block from DESIGN §4.4 with a placeholder instead of any real address: `-- insert into public.super_admins (user_id) select id from auth.users where email = '<FOUNDER_EMAIL>' on conflict do nothing;` with comment lines: paste AFTER signing up once on the deployed site; replace `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`; record the date in the HANDOFF ledger. No real email in the file.
6. **`supabase/tests/00_shim.sql`** (local-only): add, idempotently, `alter role service_role bypassrls;` (as on Supabase; `login_service()` relies on it) and `alter table storage.objects enable row level security;` (guarded via `pg_class.relrowsecurity`). `local-up.sh` skips the shim on an existing database, so drop and recreate yours once (`dropdb` through `.local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL`, then `local-up.sh`); CI starts fresh.
7. **`supabase/tests/helpers.sql`** — re-runnable (`create schema if not exists app_test`, `create or replace function`), header "test helpers — apply before `tests/rls/*.sql`; local and hosted SQL editor; never part of a migration". `grant usage on schema app_test to anon, authenticated, service_role` and `grant execute on all functions in schema app_test to anon, authenticated, service_role` at the end. Two families:
   - Fixture builders, `security definer set search_path = ''` (they bypass RLS whatever role the test currently runs as): `app_test.make_user(email text) returns uuid` (insert into `auth.users`; the 1.3a trigger creates the profile), `app_test.make_org(slug text) returns uuid` (insert `organizations` with `name = slug`, `status = 'trial'`, `trial_ends_at = now() + interval '30 days'`; the trigger creates settings, 6 groups, 4 calendars), `app_test.make_member(org uuid, uid uuid, perms public.permission_key[] default '{}') returns uuid` (active membership + permission rows), `app_test.make_fellowship(slug text, orgs uuid[]) returns uuid`, `app_test.make_household(org uuid, name text, created_via text default 'self') returns uuid`, `app_test.make_person(org uuid, hh uuid, first_name text, opts jsonb default '{}') returns uuid` (opts keys = `persons` column names, applied with `jsonb_populate_record`-style mapping), `app_test.set_setting(org uuid, col text, val text)` (dynamic `update organization_settings`), `app_test.sha256_token(token text) returns bytea` (the 1.3b convention `sha256(convert_to(token, 'UTF8'))`).
   - Session and assertion helpers, `security invoker` so RLS and grants apply to the current role: `app_test.login(uid uuid)` (`execute 'set local role authenticated'` then `set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', uid, 'role', 'authenticated', 'email', <profiles.email>)::text, true)`), `app_test.login_anon()`, `app_test.login_service()` (`set local role service_role`, claims `{role: service_role}`), `app_test.logout()` (`reset role`, clear the claims), `app_test.assert_count(label text, sql text, expected bigint)` (`execute format('select count(*) from (%s) q', sql)`), `app_test.assert_true(label text, cond boolean)`, `app_test.assert_eq(label text, actual text, expected text)`, `app_test.assert_raises(label text, sql text, sqlstate text, message_key text default null)` (`begin … exception when others`; compares `sqlstate` and, when given, `sqlerrm`; fails when nothing is raised), `app_test.assert_denied(label text, sql text)` = `assert_raises(label, sql, '42501')`. Every failure raises `test_failed` with the label in `detail`; every pass emits `raise notice 'ok: <label>'`.
8. **`scripts/db/test.sh`** (extend the 1.2 stub): `cd "$REPO_ROOT"` first (test 08 uses a relative `\i`); apply `supabase/tests/helpers.sql` with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f`; run each `supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` in name order with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -f` capturing output to a scratch log, print `PASS <file>` / `FAIL <file>` (+ last 20 log lines on failure); optional `--only <name>`; summary `N passed, M failed`; exit 1 on any failure; keep the empty-directory branch. Every test file starts with `\set ON_ERROR_STOP on` and `begin;` and ends with `rollback;` so nothing persists.
9. **`supabase/tests/rls/01_tenancy.sql`**: build orgs A and B, fellowship F containing both, users `a_member` (A, no perms), `a_manager` (A, all 12), `b_member`, `super` (insert `super_admins`), one household + person + published sermon/announcement/bulletin/document + calendar event + audience group in each org. Assertions: (1) as `a_member`, for EVERY public table with an `org_id` column (plpgsql `do` loop over `information_schema.columns`, dynamic `select count(*) from public.%I where org_id = <B>`) the count is 0, and every other public table is selectable — a recursive policy would raise 42P17 here ("no 42P17 on any table"), so collect any SQLSTATE into a failure list; (2) `a_member` sees exactly 1 row in `organizations` when B does not share with the fellowship and 2 rows after `set_setting(B, 'directory_share_in_congregation','true')` + `directory_share_with_fellowship = true` (`ca_orgs_select_fellowship`); (3) `super` sees both orgs and every table's rows; (4) `login_anon()` then `select count(*) from public.organizations` → 42501 (`assert_denied`), likewise `public.sermons`, and `select public.my_context()` → 42501; (5) `login_service()` reads both orgs (BYPASSRLS); (6) `a_manager` sees A's `notifications`, `audit_log`, `billing_customers` but none of B's.
10. **`supabase/tests/rls/08_rerunnable.sql`**: inside the transaction snapshot into a temp table the counts of tables/views/policies (per table)/triggers/functions (per schema `app`,`public`)/indexes/enum types/`storage.buckets` rows/`storage.objects` policies; then `\i supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` (the migration has no `begin`/`commit`, so it re-applies inside the test transaction); snapshot again and assert identical counts and identical policy-name sets. Then assert: every function in `app` and `public` is `prosecdef` with `search_path=` in `proconfig`; every trigger function (`pg_trigger.tgfoid`) is `prosecdef`; every public table has `relrowsecurity` true and `relforcerowsecurity` false; every policy in `public`/`storage` starts with `ca_`; `storage.objects` has exactly `ca_storage_select` and `ca_storage_insert`. Top comment: the `\i` line is psql-only — skip it in the hosted SQL editor.
11. **`supabase/tests/rls/09_grants.sql`**: (1) for every function in `public`, `has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'execute')` is false; (2) for every `public.srv_%` function, `has_function_privilege('authenticated', …)` is false and `has_function_privilege('service_role', …)` is true; (3) the set of `public` functions executable by `authenticated` equals exactly the 17 client RPC names listed in item 3 (compare sorted arrays; a new RPC must be added to both the grant and this list on purpose); (4) `anon` has zero rows in `information_schema.role_table_grants` for schema `public` and no `usage` on schema `private`; (5) `authenticated` has no `insert/update/delete` on any table of the RPC-only list in item 1 and no privilege at all on schema `private` tables; (6) `has_column_privilege('authenticated', 'public.persons', 'birthdate', 'select')` false, `… 'first_name' …` true, `households.anniversary` false, `households.hide_from_fellowship` false; (7) after `login(<member>)`: `select birthdate from public.persons` → 42501, `select * from public.persons` → 42501 (column-level), `select id, first_name from public.persons` succeeds; (8) `authenticated` can execute every helper the views and policies call (`app.household_view_level`, `app.is_adult`, `app.member_org_ids`, `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids`, `app.user_in_group`, `app.can_read_object`, `app.can_write_object`) and cannot execute `app.require_writable`, `app.rate_limit_hit`, `app.person_in_kind`, any trigger function; (9) `app_test` functions are executable by all three roles.
12. **Docs**: `docs/ENV.md` "Local database" — one line on `pnpm db:test` and `bash scripts/db/test.sh --only 09_grants`. CI needs no change (the DB job already runs the standing sequence).

## Constraints
- Migration rules (CLAUDE.md, PLAN §4, DESIGN §12): every policy `drop … if exists` then `create`; names start with `ca_`; no `force row level security`; functions untouched unless a signature must change (then drop dependents first in the same file); pgcrypto/citext schema-qualified; the file must apply twice in a row; never `supabase db push` / `db reset`; never `supabase start`.
- Policies are split per operation and use the InitPlan form (`perm_org_ids`, never per-row `app.has_perm`); never derive permissions from `auth.jwt()` claims.
- No policies for `service_role`; no grants to `anon`; no `security_invoker` on views; do not add tables, columns or RPCs (missing pieces → HANDOFF "Deviations from plan", fix in place only when a policy cannot be written otherwise).
- The `sermon-media` limit lives in exactly one place (the `c_sermon_media_limit` constant); do not repeat `2147483648` anywhere except in that comment.
- Tests: pure SQL for psql, one rolled-back transaction per file, no `\connect`, no uuids in the seed range `00000000-0000-4000-8000-…` (step 1.5), no real email addresses (`<slug>@example.test`); every shell path quoted; nothing under `/tmp`.

## Goal

## Inputs / prior state

- Steps 1.3a/1.3b fixed the names you assert on: the error-key catalogue at the top of section (5c) (keys such as `permission_denied`, `last_org_manager`, `privacy_direction_not_allowed`, `organization_suspended`, `survey_already_responded`, with SQLSTATEs 42501 / 23503 / 23505 / 22023 / P0001 — assert both); `srv_resolve_share_link` status strings (`ok`, `invalid`, `revoked`, `expired`, `max_views`, `sharing_disabled`, `unpublished`, `needs_password_reset`, `needs_password`, `wrong_password`, `rate_limited`) and its `allow_download` field; trigger names `<table>_<function>`; the audit `action` values `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` plus `invitation_permissions_dropped` and `org_without_manager`; the token convention (32 random bytes base64url; hash = `sha256(convert_to(token,'UTF8'))`).

## Build
One self-contained file per number (`<slug>@example.test` addresses only). When an assertion fails because the migration is wrong, fix the migration, not the assertion, and note it in HANDOFF.

1. **`02_permissions.sql`** — org A with: `manager` (all 12), `nobody` (no permissions) and one user per permission holding ONLY that key (`u_sermons_upload`, `u_sermons_delete`, `u_sermons_link`, `u_announcements_create`, `u_announcements_delete`, `u_announcements_edit`, `u_bulletins_upload`, `u_documents_upload`, `u_users_create`, `u_users_delete`, `u_users_edit_permissions`, `u_org_settings`); org B with its own manager (cross-check). Positive and negative case for each of the 12, in this form:
   - `sermons.upload`: holder inserts `media_kind = 'upload'` with a valid `storage_path` → ok; `nobody` → 42501 (RLS `with check`). `sermons.link`: holder inserts `media_kind = 'youtube'` with `external_url` → ok, and inserting `media_kind = 'upload'` → 42501 (PLAN: "`sermons.link` can insert youtube but not upload"); `u_sermons_upload` inserting youtube → 42501. `sermons.delete`: holder deletes a published sermon → row gone; `u_sermons_upload` deleting → 0 rows affected, row still present (`assert_count`).
   - `announcements.create` / `.edit` / `.delete`: insert / update title / delete, each ok for its holder and denied (42501 on insert; 0 rows affected on update/delete) for `nobody` and for the holders of the other two keys. `bulletins.upload`, `documents.upload`: insert ok / 42501; update and delete by the same holder ok; `nobody` reads published rows but not drafts (`publish_at` in the future).
   - `users.create`: `create_invitation(A, 'new@example.test', null, '{}')` ok for the holder; `nobody` → `permission_denied`; holder with perms `'{sermons.upload}'` → `permission_denied` with detail `users.edit_permissions` (PLAN: "`users.create`-only cannot mint an invitation with permissions"); `manager` with perms → ok. `users.edit_permissions`: `set_membership_permissions(<nobody's membership>, '{sermons.link}')` ok for the holder and visible as 1 row in `org_membership_permissions`; `u_users_create` → `permission_denied`. `users.delete`: `set_membership_status(<membership>, 'disabled')` ok for the holder, `nobody` → `permission_denied`; `remove_membership` ok / denied; re-enabling (`'active'`) needs `users.create` (`u_users_delete` → `permission_denied`). `org.settings`: `update organization_settings set sermons_shareable = true` → 1 row for the holder, 0 rows for `nobody`; `directory_share_with_fellowship = true` while `directory_share_in_congregation = false` → SQLSTATE `23514` (check).
   - Last manager (PLAN: "last manager cannot be stripped"): make `u_users_edit_permissions` and `manager` the only two `users.edit_permissions` holders; strip `manager` → ok; then `set_membership_permissions(<u_users_edit_permissions>, '{}')` by that same user → `last_org_manager` (P0001); `set_membership_status(<that membership>, 'disabled')` by `u_users_delete` → `last_org_manager`; `remove_membership` → `last_org_manager`; a direct `delete from org_membership_permissions` as `login_service()` → `last_org_manager` too (trigger, not policy).
   - Escalation via invitation (DESIGN §12 "escalation via invitation"): `manager` creates an invitation for `invitee@example.test` with perms `'{sermons.upload}'`; another manager strips `manager`'s `users.edit_permissions`; `invitee` (user created with that email) calls `accept_invitation(token)` → membership active, 0 permissions, one `audit_log` row with `action = 'invitation_permissions_dropped'`; a second `accept_invitation` with the same token → `invitation_invalid`; a user with a different email → `invitation_email_mismatch`.
   - Cross-org: B's manager cannot see or change A's memberships (`set_membership_permissions` on an A membership → `permission_denied` or `membership_not_found`; assert whichever 1.3b raises and note it).
2. **`03_directory_visibility.sql`** — fellowship F = {A, B, C}; org D outside F. Settings: A and B share in congregation and with fellowship; C shares in congregation only; D shares with fellowship (but is not in F). Users: `a_member` (A, no perms), `b_member`, `b_admin` (B, `users.create` only — a directory admin by decision 4), `b_settings` (B, `org.settings` only — also a directory admin), `b_head` (B, no perms, linked to the head of household H1), `b_spouse` (linked to H1's spouse), `super`. Households in B, each with adults and where noted children: H1 (normal: head, spouse, child aged 8 with birthdate, `show_children_in_fellowship = false`), H2 (`hide_from_fellowship = true`), H3 (`hide_from_congregation = true`), H4 (`show_children_in_fellowship = true`, one child aged 10), H5 (`created_via = 'admin'` — must default to `hide_from_fellowship = true`), H6 (adult with `directory_listed = false`, adult `congregation_status = 'inactive'`, adult with `deceased_on` set), H7 (person `household_role = 'other'` with no birthdate; adult with `birthdate_visibility = 'full'`; adult with `'hidden'`). One household each in A, C and D. Assertions (use `directory_persons` / `directory_households` unless stated):
   - `a_member` (fellowship level) sees from B exactly the adults of H1, H4 and H7's full/hidden adults, plus H4's child; NOT H1's child (adults-only), not H2/H3/H5, not the unlisted/inactive/deceased persons of H6, not H7's role-`other`-without-birthdate person (DESIGN §4.3: "excluded from fellowship view"); not C's household (no fellowship sharing) nor D's (not in F). `view_level = 'fellowship'` on every B row; `birthdate` is null; `birthday_display` is `MM-DD` for `month_day` and `full` visibility and null for `hidden`; `anniversary_display` on `directory_households` is null at fellowship level, `MM-DD` for `b_member`, `YYYY-MM-DD` for `b_head` (own household) and `b_admin` (decision 2: no anniversary year outside the congregation); `hide_from_fellowship`/`hide_from_congregation`/`show_children_in_fellowship`/`privacy_confirmed_at` columns are null for `a_member` and `b_member`, populated for `b_head` and `b_admin`.
   - `b_member` (congregation level) sees H1, H2, H4, H5 (hidden-from-fellowship does not hide from the congregation), H7; not H3 (`hide_from_congregation`), not the unlisted/inactive/deceased persons; `birthday_display` is `YYYY-MM-DD` for `full`, `MM-DD` for `month_day`, null for `hidden`; `birthdate`, `member_since`, `youth_override` are null. After `set_setting(B, 'directory_share_in_congregation', 'false')` (and `directory_share_with_fellowship = false` first, to satisfy the check) `b_member` sees only their own household and `a_member` sees nothing from B.
   - `b_head` sees every person of H1 including the child, with `birthdate`, `view_level = 'household'`; `b_admin` and `b_settings` see every household and person of B including H3 and H6's hidden persons (`view_level = 'admin'`), with `member_since` and `youth_override`; `super` sees everything in every org.
   - Column-level: after `login(b_member)`, `select birthdate from public.persons` → 42501, `select anniversary from public.households` → 42501, `select * from public.persons` → 42501; `select count(*) from public.persons` (base table, allowed columns only) equals the count from `directory_persons` for that viewer (PLAN §5: base-table policy = view rule).
   - Direction rule (founder decision 1): `b_admin` calls `set_household_privacy(H1, true, false, false)` → ok (more private); then `set_household_privacy(H1, false, false, false)` → `privacy_direction_not_allowed` (42501); `b_admin` setting `show_children_in_fellowship` true→false ok, false→true denied; `b_head` may set every flag in both directions and `privacy_confirmed_by = b_head`, `privacy_confirmed_at is not null` afterwards; `b_spouse` likewise; `b_member` (not in H1) → `not_household_editor`; `super` any direction. H5 (`created_via = 'admin'`) has `hide_from_fellowship = true` without anyone touching it (PLAN: "admin-created household hidden from fellowship by default") and `b_head`-style adult of H5 can flip it to false.
   - Minors and accounts: `save_person` linking `user_id` to H1's child → `minor_cannot_have_account` (P0001); `b_head` setting `congregation_status = 'member'` on the spouse via `save_person` → `field_not_editable` (42501); `b_admin` doing it via `set_congregation_status` → ok; `b_head` may edit own contact fields via `save_person`; a second person with `household_role = 'head'` in H1 → 23505.
   - Leader notes: `b_admin` `save_leader_notes('household', H1, 'x')` ok and readable by `b_settings`; `b_head` → `permission_denied`/42501 on the RPC and 0 rows from `household_leader_notes`; `a_member` 0 rows.
   - Org status: `update organizations set status = 'suspended' where id = B` (as service) → `a_member` sees no B households and no B row in `organizations`; back to `active` → visible again.
3. **`04_sermons_share_links.sql`** — org S with `linker` (`sermons.link`), `uploader` (`sermons.upload`), `member` (none); one published upload sermon `sermon_up` (`storage_path = S/sermons/<id>/a.mp3`), one published youtube sermon `sermon_yt`, one draft. Sequence: `sermons_shareable` false → `create_share_link(sermon_up, 'l', 'password-12', null, null)` by `linker` → `sharing_disabled`; `set_setting(S, 'sermons_shareable', 'true')`; `member` → `permission_denied`; `linker` on the draft → `sermon_not_published`; `linker` with a 7-character password → `password_too_short`; with null password while `sermon_share_requires_password` → `password_required`; `uploader` creates a link with `'password-12'` → returns `{link_id, token}`; the token is 43 characters; `sermon_share_links` shows `requires_password = true`, `view_count = 0`; `member` selects 0 rows from `sermon_share_links`, `linker` 1 row; `private.share_link_secrets` is unreadable for `authenticated` (42501). Then `login_service()` with `h := app_test.sha256_token(token)`, `ip := 'iphash-1'`: `srv_resolve_share_link(h, null, ip) ->> 'status'` = `needs_password`; wrong password → `wrong_password` and `view_count` still 0; 9 more wrong attempts → the 11th call (any password) → `rate_limited` (PLAN: "10 wrong passwords lock the token"), also for the correct password; a fresh token on another link with a different `ip` still works (limits are per token hash and per ip hash); correct password on an unlocked token → `ok`, `view_count = 1`, `allow_download = false`, `sermon.media_kind = 'upload'`, `org.slug` present; `set_setting(S, 'sermon_share_allow_download', 'true')` → `allow_download = true` for the upload link and `false` for a link on `sermon_yt` (founder decision 5: uploaded media only); a link created with `max_views = 1` → second `ok`… → `max_views`; a link with `expires_at = now() - interval '1 minute'` → `expired`; `revoke_share_link` by `linker` → `revoked` (and `member` → `permission_denied`); `set_setting(S, 'sermons_shareable', 'false')` → `sharing_disabled` for a valid link (PLAN: "share link fails after org disables sharing"); re-enable and `update sermons set publish_at = null` → `unpublished`; `set_setting(S, 'sermon_share_requires_password', 'false')`, create a passwordless link, then set it back to true → `needs_password_reset`; unknown hash → `invalid`; `login(member)` then `srv_resolve_share_link(...)` → 42501; `login_anon()` → 42501. Assert an `audit_log` row exists for the share-link insert and for the revoke.
4. **`05_audiences.sql`** + **`packages/domain/fixtures/persons.json`** — create the fixture first (shared with step 1.6's Vitest; not under `src/`). Shape: `{ "settings": { "timezone": "America/New_York", "youth_min_age": 13, "youth_max_age": 25, "adult_min_age": 18, "youth_excludes_married": true, "adult_groups_include_youth": true }, "persons": [ { "key": "…", "first_name": "…", "sex": "male"|"female"|null, "age_years": <int|null>, "birthday_offset_days": <int, default 0>, "marital_status": "…", "household_role": "…", "congregation_status": "…", "deceased": false, "youth_override": null|true|false, "in_custom_group": false, "expected": { "everyone": bool, "members": bool, "attendees": bool, "youth": bool, "men": bool, "women": bool, "custom": bool } } ] }`. Ages are relative so the test never rots: birthdate = (today in the org timezone) − `age_years` years − `birthday_offset_days` days; `birthday_offset_days = -1` with `age_years = 13` means "turns 13 tomorrow" (still 12). ## Constraints

- Do not change the fixture shape once written without updating this step's notes in HANDOFF — step 1.6's Vitest suite depends on it.

- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

## Build

## Constraints
- The seed is local-only and must never be applied by `local-up.sh` or CI automatically; it must apply cleanly on a database that has had `9999_init.sql` applied twice and the RLS tests run (tests roll back, so the DB is empty). It must not bypass triggers (no `alter table … disable trigger`) — if a guard rejects seed data, the seed data is wrong or the guard is, and either fix goes to HANDOFF.
- No real email addresses, no real push tokens, no real YouTube/Dropbox content beyond syntactically valid example URLs; the seed share-link password is a local convenience, labelled as such.
- `gen-types.sh` must not require Docker, must not modify anything but `packages/db/src/database.types.ts`, and must produce byte-identical output on a second run (CI drift check). Never `supabase db push`/`db reset`/`start`.
- Do not write `packages/db/src/{client,rpc,keys}.ts`, queries, `packages/domain/src/*` or any web code (steps 1.6/1.7). Do not edit `9999_init.sql` unless the seed exposes a genuine bug (record it). No npm dependencies (the CLI runs via `npx`).
- Docs must describe the repo as it is: every policy, RPC, error key and script name copied from the files, not from memory.

## Verify
- Standing sequence `scripts/db/local-up.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh && scripts/db/test.sh` → exit 0, `9 passed`.
- `pnpm db:seed` → `seed applied` notice with the share token and the notification count; running it again → returns early without error; `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select count(*) from public.organizations where slug like 'seed-%'"` → `3`; `select count(*) from public.persons` ≥ 30; `select count(*) from public.households h where not exists (select 1 from public.persons p where p.household_id = h.id and p.household_role = 'head')` → `0`; `select count(*) from public.notifications` ≥ 3; `select hide_from_fellowship from public.households where created_via = 'admin'` → all `t`.
- Seed visibility spot-check inside `begin … rollback` using `app_test.login(<grace-member uid>)`: `select count(*) from public.directory_households` > 0 and excludes the `hide_from_congregation` household; as `<hope-member>` `select count(*) from public.directory_persons where org_id = <seed-grace>` > 0 and contains no minors except the `show_children_in_fellowship` family.
- `pnpm db:seed` against a non-local `DATABASE_URL` (e.g. `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://x@db.example.test/x pnpm db:seed`) → refuses with a clear message and exit 1.
- `pnpm db:types` → writes `packages/db/src/database.types.ts`; a second run leaves `git diff --exit-code packages/db/src/database.types.ts` clean; `grep -c "sermon_share_allow_download" packages/db/src/database.types.ts` ≥ 1; the `permission_key` enum union contains 12 members.
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green (the generated file is ignored by ESLint, compiled by tsc); `pnpm format:check` clean.
- `docs/RLS.md` policy table row count equals `select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname in ('public','storage')`; every error key in the 1.3b catalogue appears in `docs/RLS.md`; `grep -riE "pro (plan )?recommended" HANDOFF.md supabase/README.md docs/MIGRATIONS.md docs/RLS.md` → no matches.
- After the push, the CI types-drift step runs (guard satisfied) and passes.
